$comment: Legal status transitions and their field side effects. Anything not listed under transitions is rejected with 409 and the error body below. This table is the whole state machine. Do not add states.

transitions.requires: priority is set OR due_at is set

on_violation.message: set a priority or a due date before promoting

transitions.note: Quick-complete from the inbox is legal and common.
Demotion to inbox is not a thing. Drop it or edit it.

side_effects.on: transition to done where the task belongs to a series with mode=after_completion
side_effects.generates: the next instance, due at completion time plus the rule interval
side_effects.note: The new instance is a new task row with a new id and num, linked to the same series.

side_effects.on: transition to done where the task belongs to a series with mode=fixed
side_effects.generates: nothing at completion time. The scheduler generates the next instance when the rule fires.

side_effects.does_not: delete or modify an instance already generated by after_completion
side_effects.note: Reopening after the next instance exists leaves you with two open tasks. That is correct and intentional.

side_effects.on: complete a parent with open children
side_effects.note: The client shows a prompt. The server never cascades on its own.

side_effects.rejects_when: status is done or dropped, with 409

side_effects.note: This is what makes the task eligible for a new reminder.

side_effects.writes: one row to event with actor, task_id, kind, and a patch
side_effects.note: No mutation path skips the event log. /undo depends on it and so does the activity feed.

undo.depth: unbounded, walking the event log backwards
undo.scope: the calling actor's own events only
undo.note: Undo writes its own event of kind undo, referencing the seq it reversed. A second undo call reverses the next-oldest eligible event, not the undo itself.
